newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SOCCER-POLICE TO STEP UP SECURITY AT MATCH IN HONG KONG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-POLICE TO STEP UP SECURITY AT MATCH IN HONG KONG.

text.p: Hong Kong police will step up
security at a soccer match between Japanese and Hong Kong sides
on Sunday because of a dispute over islands in the East China
Sea, Hong Kong's TVB news said on Thursday.
TVB news quoted a senior officer as saying police would
increase manpower at the Hong Kong stadium to prevent a possible
flare-up of violence between Japanese and Hong Kong fans.
The officer also said they would segregate fans from the two
sides.
Hong Kong police officials were not immediately available
for comment.
Hong Kong's South China club and Japan's Grampus Eight meet
on Sunday in the Asian Cup Winners' Cup.
Anti-Japanese sentiment in Hong Kong has flared in recent
months after Japanese extremists erected a lighthouse and flags
on the disputed islands, which Japan calls the Senkakus and
which China claims as the Diaoyu isles.
Tension reached a new high last week when Hong Kong protest
leader David Chan drowned after jumping off a ship in the area.
Japan has claimed the territory, a cluster of uninhabited
rocky islets, since 1895. China has claimed them for centuries.
Taiwan also lays claim to the territory.
